daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Three political parties have signaled support for Sugiono as President Prabowo's choice for vice president, with Amran Sulaiman and Sugiono named as the two leading candidates. The selection process, described by MUI Deputy Chair as requiring honesty and fairness, represents what Basarah described as a first in Indonesia's history. Kompas reports the strengthening of Hambalang Boys in the vice presidential selection.

  • National Police Chief Listyo Sigit refused to attend an ethics hearing, prompting concerns about his integrity from DPR member Sahroni.
  • The KPK revealed that Klaten Regent Hamenang misused district funds to pay legislator honoraria at district events and abused authority to pursue a MURI record for mass chicken soup consumption.
  • Lieutenant General Widi Prasetijono was sentenced to five years in prison and dismissed from the military in a land corruption case.
  • Police Commissioner Iman Imanuddin, a treason suspect, was subjected to an ethics trial related to orders given during his tenure as Dirreskrimum Polda Metro.
  • Bareskrim named General Listyo Sigit and others as treason suspects, reportedly linked to involvement in large demonstrations.
  • Jimly Asshiddiqie stated that the vice presidential vacancy provides momentum to evaluate the 1945 Constitution and establish emergency state regulations.
  • President Prabowo has praised Police Chief Suyudi three times in two weeks, with the latest commendation stating the police are "on the right track".
  • The government explained to the Constitutional Court about financing for Wantimpres members.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia ruled out joining the Mecca Defence Pact, citing its free and active foreign policy. The Foreign Ministry reaffirmed Indonesia's independent stance on international military alliances. This position underscores Jakarta's long-standing principle of non-alignment in global security arrangements.

  • Indonesia urged protection for Rohingya following the International Court of Justice genocide ruling against Myanmar.
  • Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates strengthened economic partnership as the two countries mark 50 years of diplomatic relations, with the UAE reaffirming its commitment to strategic partnership.
  • Indonesia and Kuwait strengthened cooperation in energy and investment sectors.
  • Indonesia called for peaceful resolution of the Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen.
  • Indonesia welcomed U.S. support for national nuclear development.

Other

The United States imposed new tariffs on Indonesia shortly after President-elect Trump praised Prabowo as a "great leader," with the proposed 18 percent tariff prompting Indonesia to push export diversification and pursue dialogue with Washington. Indonesia is also curbing finished-goods imports to boost local industry. Meanwhile, Nvidia halted chip shipments to Indonesia and three other Southeast Asian countries.

  • President Prabowo targets up to four interactive panels per school by end of 2026 and launched Studio Guru to broadcast quality lessons to all schools, while teacher allowances reached Rp 70.64 trillion by November.
  • The government opened CPNS 2026 registration with 154,000 positions available, including 70,000 positions at the Forestry Ministry prioritizing forest police and Manggala Agni firefighters.
  • An INA-backed plasma plant will cut medicine prices by up to 24.6 percent.
  • Central Java Governor Ahmad Luthfi announced 2027 minimum wages for the province.
  • The rupiah weakened toward Rp 18,370, with economists highlighting concerns over expected MSCI capital outflows.
